reading: A one-colour shape has a colour-2 segment attached to one side; the shape is reflected across the edge it shares with the 2s (the reflection overwrites the 2s), and the background becomes 3.
why: output = shape plus its reflection about the line between the shape and its 2-marker; all other cells are 3

reading: Every row whose interior (all cells except the first and last) is entirely background, and every such column, has its background cells painted 3.

new_rows.name: lane
new_rows.datalog:
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rowz(Y, count(X)) :- px(Y, X, 0), wmax(W), X > 0, X < W.
fullrow(Y) :- rowz(Y, N), wmax(W), N = W - 1.
colz(X, count(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 0), hmax(H), Y > 0, Y < H.
fullcol(X) :- colz(X, N), hmax(H), N = H - 1.
lane(Y, X) :- fullrow(Y), px(Y, X, 0).
lane(Y, X) :- fullcol(X), px(Y, X, 0).

why: exactly the 0-cells of fully clear interior rows/columns become 3

reading: A path of 3 grows from the green 2-cell segment along its axis, turning 90 degrees whenever the next cell is an 8, until it reaches the red 2-cell segment.

slots.start: the 2-cell colour-3 segment (its axis gives the initial direction, toward the target)
slots.obstacle: colour-8 cells, which force a 90-degree turn

why: the 3-path is connected, never crosses an 8, and turns only in front of an 8, ending adjacent to the red segment

reading: Each row has one main colour (its most common non-background colour); cells of that colour become background and every other cell of the row (background or noise) becomes the main colour.

slots.main: the row's most common non-0 colour

why: per row, output = main colour exactly where the input is not main colour

reading: Each colour-9 object carries a two-cell-wide 6/9 checker band across its middle; the object is cut between the two band lines, the 6s are erased, and the two halves move apart by one cell each, perpendicular to the band.

slots.subject: each object containing 6s
slots.cut: the line between the two band rows/columns
slots.shift: each half moves one cell away from the cut

why: each half keeps its 9-cells' shape; the halves are separated by a 2-cell gap where the cut was

reading: Each coloured cell gets a 2 at its up-left diagonal neighbour (wrapping around the grid edges, only onto background), then the grid is tiled 3x3.

new_rows.name: upleft
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
upleft(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y > 0, X > 0, Y2 = Y - 1, X2 = X - 1, px(Y2, X2, 0).
upleft(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0, X > 0, hmax(Y2), X2 = X - 1, px(Y2, X2, 0).
upleft(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y > 0, X = 0, Y2 = Y - 1, wmax(X2), px(Y2, X2, 0).
upleft(Y2, X2) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0, X = 0, hmax(Y2), wmax(X2), px(Y2, X2, 0).

why: output is 3x3 copies of the input with 2 added at the toroidal up-left of every coloured cell
invariants: original coloured cells in every copy

reading: Keep only the single cell whose colour occurs exactly once, surround it with a 3x3 ring of 2, and clear everything else.

new_rows.name: uniq
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
uniq(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), N = 1.

why: output is all 0 except the unique-colour cell and its 8 neighbours, which are 2
invariants: position and colour of the unique cell

reading: Empty (all-background) squares of side 3, and side-2 squares that do not overlap a side-3 one, are filled with 1.
why: 1-cells are exactly the union of largest-first non-overlapping empty squares of side >= 2

reading: Each colour-1 shape is classified: closed shapes (solid or with an enclosed hole) turn 2 and slide to the left border; shapes whose outline has a gap turn 3 and slide to the right border, keeping their rows.

slots.subject: each colour-1 object
slots.test: closed outline/solid vs outline with an opening
slots.closed: recolour 2, move left to the border
slots.open: recolour 3, move right to the border

why: every object keeps its shape and row span, touches the left (2) or right (3) border, and the rest is background 4

reading: Inside the bounding box of the colour-8 cells, every 1 becomes 3.

new_rows.name: inbox8
new_rows.datalog:
ya(min(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
yb(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
xa(min(X)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
xb(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
inbox8(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 1), ya(A), yb(B), xa(L), xb(R), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= L, X <= R.

why: exactly the 1-cells within the 8-box change, to 3
